title: Liturgical Calendar Validations Path
description: The source data this API can be asked to validate. Clients iterate this list and send back an item's opaque id, so no filesystem path crosses the wire.

id.description: Opaque identifier a client sends back to request this check.

region.description: Null when the item applies to its whole rite; an ISO nation code when it applies only to that nation's calendar.

schema.description: Bare filename of the JSON schema this item validates against, resolvable under /schemas.

steps.description: The ordered checks this item passes through when validated. A frame's own `step` field carries these same values (`exists`, `parses`, `validates`), plus a fourth, `complete`, that marks the terminal frame and is not a check. Read `step` on each frame to know what it is about; stop watching a check when a frame arrives whose `step` is `complete`, not when you have counted `steps.length` frames. The terminal `complete` frame is sent only in reply to a request that carried a `requestId`: it is a new frame rather than a new field, so it is gated on the v2 opt-in signal to keep a frame-counting v1 client from miscounting. A client that stops on `complete` must send a `requestId` on every request. This array's length remains an upper bound rather than an exact per-check frame count -- a file whose JSON fails to decode stops after `parses` and never emits `validates` -- but that no longer matters for phase completion, because `complete` is explicit. See https://github.com/Liturgical-Calendar/LiturgicalCalendarAPI/issues/821: the length was always an upper bound, and now nothing waits for it to be exact. See https://github.com/Liturgical-Calendar/LiturgicalCalendarAPI/issues/819, closed by this work: these step names now reach the wire as the frame's own `step` field, so there is no second vocabulary left to relate them to.
